sovereign_country.strategic_role: 全球跨境基金设立第一大国、超大型跨国投资架构

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Consumer Polling and Cross-Border Market Research Platform

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–United States Double Taxation Treaty (signed 1996, effective 2001)
Luxembourg–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 1987, entered into force 1988)
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) investment protection agreements

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) and amending the AML/CFT framework; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019 on the RBE; EU Directives 2015/849 (4AMLD) and 2018/843 (5AMLD) as transposed; CSSF AML/CFT regulations and guidance for supervised entities.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of the general partner's passport (biometric page)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Passport-issuing authority of the partner's state of nationality
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if the issuing state is not a Hague Convention member)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Proof of residential address (utility bill or bank statement)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider or financial institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization as applicable

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / police clearance from country(ies) of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Judicial or police authority of the issuing state
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization for non-Hague member states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming professional reputation and source of wealth/funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Issuing bank or licensed financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or Consular Legalization if required by Luxembourg authorities)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based screening against PEP lists (domestic and foreign), UN Security Council sanctions, EU consolidated sanctions, OFAC sanctions (where contractually applicable), and Luxembourg national freezing lists. Screening must occur at initiation and on a continuous basis via automated monitoring; simplified due diligence may apply for low-risk market research SaaS, but PEP and sanctions screening cannot be waived.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), consolidated, Articles 944-1 to 944-17 governing the Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp), as amended by the Law of 12 July 2013; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies and RESA; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 January 2003 on RCS filings.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés), operated on the official LBR electronic portal (www.lbr.lu) under the supervision of the Ministry of Justice.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif / partnership agreement (contrat de société) executed by private writing unless real property is contributed, in which case a notarial deed is mandatory; the instrument is lodged electronically with the RCS using the standard e-filing declaration of creation for an SCSp.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The SCSp may be incorporated with no minimum statutory capital; the partnership agreement freely determines the capital commitments of the partners, and no escrow account or paid-up capital deposit is required by Luxembourg law.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the General Partner hereby adopts the partnership agreement, records the capital commitments subscribed by the partners, and directs the execution of all formation documents of the SCSp. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the registered office of the SCSp is fixed at [address], Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and that all legal notices shall be served at this address. FURTHER RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed as Manager, with authority to represent the SCSp and open bank accounts. FURTHER RESOLVED, that the Manager is authorised to file the RCS registration, obtain tax and VAT numbers, register beneficial ownership, and complete post-registration declarations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers - RCS electronic name search and reservation desk (www.lbr.lu / www.rcs.lu)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct exact-match and full-text searches on the RCS database to confirm that the proposed SCSp name is distinctive, lawful, and not identical or confusingly similar to an existing legal entity, association, or trade mark registered in Luxembourg; optionally reserve the approved name with the RCS against payment of the applicable reservation fee.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate name and secondary identifying statement
Identity document of the General Partner and each limited partner
Name reservation application form (if reservation is requested)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS rejects the name because of identity or resemblance, the partners may immediately propose an alternative name and resubmit the reservation; no formal administrative appeal is available against a preliminary name refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (mandatory only where real estate is contributed) or all partners by private deed; advanced eIDAS electronic signature is accepted
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the SCSp partnership agreement in English, French, or German, setting out the corporate name, registered office, purpose (consumer polling and cross-border market research SaaS), the identity and liability limits of the limited partners, the management powers of the General Partner, contribution amounts, profit-sharing rules, transfer restrictions, and termination events; sign the instrument either before a Luxembourg notary or by private deed with authenticated signatures.
required_dossiers: Draft partnership agreement (contrat de société)
Passport or national ID copies of all partners
Notarized powers of attorney where a partner is represented
Up-to-date extract of the corporate register of any corporate partner
Anti-money laundering and ultimate beneficial owner declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a signing defect or invalid power of attorney is identified, the partners must re-execute the instrument or procure a new legalized power of attorney; any defect in consent under Articles 1119 to 1122 of the Civil Code requires fresh unanimous execution or rectification before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration of the SCSp with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: RCS - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés, Luxembourg Business Registers (electronic filing via the LBR eDesk portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the RCS creation file electronically together with the executed partnership agreement and a signed statement of the General Partner confirming the accuracy of the filed particulars; pay the statutory e-filing fee and indicate the date of the constitutive act; registration must be applied for within one month of the execution of the partnership agreement.
required_dossiers: Executed partnership agreement
RCS electronic declaration of creation (form C - SCSp)
Statement on registered office address with occupancy title
Identity documents of the General Partner and Managers
Acceptance letters of appointed Managers
Proof of payment of the e-filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a demand for supplementary documents or a query, the filer must cure the deficiency within the indicated one-month grace period by uploading the missing exhibits through the same eDesk file; failure to do so leads to rejection, requiring a fresh filing and a new fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the constitutive act in RESA
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA), published electronically by the RCS under the Law of 19 December 2002
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Following RCS registration, the registry automatically transmits the statutory extract of the partnership agreement for publication in RESA within the prescribed delay; the General Partner must verify the published text and obtain certified copies for banking, tax, and contractual counterparty purposes.
required_dossiers: No active filing is required from the applicant - the RCS initiates RESA publication
Optional: request for certified copy of RESA publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA extract is inaccurate or omits mandatory statutory particulars, the General Partner must file a corrective appendix with the RCS within 10 business days so that the registry issues a rectified publication.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-registration tax, beneficial ownership, and data protection filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) maintained by the Luxembourg Business Registers; Commission Nationale pour la Protection des Données (CNPD)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the national tax number (NIF) automatically or via the ACD; assess whether VAT registration with the AEDT is required for B2B and B2C supplies of market-research and SaaS services; register the beneficial owners of the SCSp in the RBE within one month of incorporation; designate and register a data protection officer and prepare the record of processing activities with the CNPD in accordance with the GDPR and the amended Law of 1 August 2018 on data protection.
required_dossiers: RCS registration certificate and RESA publication extract
Partnership agreement and identity documents of beneficial owners
RBE filing form listing all ultimate beneficial owners
VAT registration form (form 640/1) if taxable turnover threshold is met
CNPD registration of the controller and data protection officer
GDPR record of processing activities for the consumer panel database
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late RBE filings attract fixed fines between EUR 250 and EUR 1,250; if such penalty is applied, the filer should mount a written mitigation request to the RBE registrar together with the completed declaration; VAT or NIF issues are cured by filing an out-of-time application with the AEDT/ACD and paying any assessed late payment interest.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction générale Industrie, Innovation et Commerce (no prior authorization is required for non-regulated online market-research and polling services under Luxembourg commercial law)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not applicable - the activity is an unlicensed service business (ISIC 7320 / NAICS 541910); RCS registration is the sole statutory formal requirement, and the operator must separately discharge payroll, CNPD-GDPR, and data-processing obligations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environment Agency), Ministry of the Environment, Climate and Biodiversity
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt - Category observation only; the consumer-panel SaaS activity is not listed in Annex II of the Law of 15 May 2018 on environmental impact assessment, and no screening threshold is crossed; no environmental permit is required.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No production wastewater, VOC, or process-emission limits apply to the nominal office-based activity; sanitary wastewater discharges must respect commune sewer by-laws (generally pH 6.5-9.5, COD below 1,500 mg/L); electrical and electronic waste (WEEE) must be collected in compliance with Directive 2012/19/EU and the national Law of 24 March 2023 on waste management.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire-safety clearance for the registered office and any server or co-location area must be obtained from the competent municipal fire brigade (Administration de la protection civile); a structural load certificate is required for any on-premises IT racks; occupational health and safety compliance with the Luxembourg Labor Code (Article L.312-1) is verified by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM), and employees must be registered with the Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS) for social security coverage.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD / Luxembourg Inland Revenue) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; consolidated e-portal: guichet.lu / MyGuichet.lu.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Register the SCSp with the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via notarial e-filing on MyGuichet.lu; obtain RCS registration number; file VAT registration form (Formulaire 1050) with AEDT through MyGuichet; non-established foreign entities must appoint a Luxembourg VAT representative (jointly and severally liable) unless covered by the One-Stop-Shop (OSS) scheme; the 13-character VAT identification number (LU + 8 digits) is issued within 2-4 weeks; no minimum capital requirement and no registration deposit apply to the SCSp.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - the SCSp is fiscally transparent under Luxembourg law: not subject to corporate income tax (CIT), municipal business tax (IBT), or net wealth tax at entity level; profits, gains and credits are allocated to partners and taxed at partner level; for VAT purposes the SCSp is nonetheless treated as an independent taxable person carrying out economic activities.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No Luxembourg check-the-box election exists; fiscal transparency of the SCSp is mandatory under the Law of 12 July 2013 and cannot be waived - the SCSp cannot elect to be treated as a taxable corporation for direct tax purposes; partners may, however, obtain confirmatory rulings or advance pricing agreements (APA) to clarify cross-border hybrid classification; ATAD 2 anti-hybrid rules (Law of 21 December 2019) override any divergent foreign characterization and prevent double non-taxation.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 small-business exemption threshold (Art. 57 VAT Law, ex-VAT turnover) for resident businesses; no threshold applies to non-established suppliers - VAT registration is mandatory before the first taxable transaction; separate thresholds apply to distance sales and OSS (EUR 10,000 for cross-border pan-EU B2C e-services and sales of goods) and to intra-Community consignments (EUR 100,000).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or mandatory B2B e-invoicing regime is currently in force in Luxembourg; B2G invoices must be transmitted electronically in PEPPOL/UBL format; voluntary B2B e-invoicing compliant with EN 16931 (Factur-X) is permitted via the AEDT portal and APIs; mandatory B2B e-invoicing is expected upon transposition of the EU ViDA ('VAT in the Digital Age') rules, projected no earlier than 2030.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Supplies of the consumer-panel survey platform to B2B customers established outside Luxembourg are outside Luxembourg VAT scope under the Article 44 place-of-supply rule (reverse charge in the customer's jurisdiction); B2C electronically supplied services to EU consumers are taxable in the customer's Member State under Article 58 and reportable via OSS - effectively zero Luxembourg VAT on exports; exports of tangible goods (e.g., research samples, incentive items) to non-EU destinations qualify for the 0% exemption provided dispatch outside the EU is proven within 90 days of supply.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document / e-Douane clearance)
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note
Inward Remittance Certificate / SWIFT MT103 proof of payment
Commercial invoice and signed client acceptance / service certificate
Recipient VAT registration proof (for EU B2B supplies) or proof of physical dispatch outside the EU (for goods)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg courts and AEDT may claw back falsely zero-rated output VAT with default interest of 0.6% per month plus compensatory interest; administrative fines up to EUR 3,500 per infringement apply to minor formal errors, while fraudulent conduct triggers fines up to EUR 10,000 and imprisonment up to 5 years under the General Tax Law and the VAT Act; abusive claims lead to retrospective reassessments, disallowance of input VAT deduction, publication of the sanction, and in cross-border cases joint liability of the partners and VAT representative.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) acting in coordination with the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance; the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) supervises banking, fintech, and electronic money institution licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a fully liberalised euro-area jurisdiction with no general foreign-exchange controls. Both current-account and capital-account transactions are freely convertible under the EU Capital Movements Directive (88/361/EEC) and the Luxembourg Law of 5 August 1993 on the financial sector. Profit remittances and partnership distributions from an SCSp are unrestricted and may be paid to non-resident partners without prior BCL authorisation, provided that mandatory anti-money laundering and beneficial-owner verification requirements are satisfied by the paying bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, mandatory conversion, or repatriation timeline for export proceeds or cross-border service receipts. Export and market-research revenues may be retained in EUR or any foreign currency, converted, or hedged freely; however, banks will require supporting commercial documentation and accurate payment purpose codes for anti-money laundering transaction monitoring.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. PayPal and Wise, operating as CSSF-registered or EU-passported electronic money institutions (EMIs), are legally available for low-value mass payouts to consumer survey participants and cross-border market-research remuneration. They are not substitutes for a full tier-1 Luxembourg corporate bank account for high-value inbound capital injections, commercial trade settlements, standby letters of credit, or complex liquidity management. Legal constraints include operational caps on aggregate balances, mandatory client-fund safeguarding, transaction-threshold reporting, and the need for underlying commercial documentation to avoid being treated as a money-transfer or payment-services intermediary without a proper licence.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For tier-1 Luxembourg banks, initial onboarding normally requires at least one director, partner, or duly appointed authorised signatory with power of attorney to appear physically at a bank branch or before a Luxembourg-based notary for identity verification. The CSSF AML/CFT framework does not absolutely prohibit remote onboarding, but banks may permit fully remote opening only where certified video-identification technology is used and supplemented by apostilled corporate documents, sworn declarations, and direct confirmation from the Luxembourg Trade Register. For an SCSp with non-resident UBOs, the practical mandate is a physical or notarised KYC interview for the ultimate beneficial owners, with a power-of-attorney file lodged for day-to-day signatories.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial owner residing in a high-risk third-country jurisdiction or with opaque source-of-funds history.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UBS extract from the Luxembourg RCS confirming UBO declaration, apostilled and sworn passport copies, independent source-of-wealth letters (bank statements, sale deeds, audited financials), a legal opinion on the intermediate holding chain, and a notarised declaration of ownership.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp statute creating a pass-through partnership with unclear liability and UBO transparency.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified copy of the limited partnership agreement, RCS registration and UBO register extract, CSSF-registered beneficial-owner filing, a Luxembourg legal opinion confirming the SCSp has separate legal personality and contractual capacity, and the notarised appointment of the general partner.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity digital transactions from a consumer polling platform that may resemble money laundering or unlicensed payment processing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed transaction-flow narrative, source platform contracts and commercial agreements, audited business plan and projected volumes, KYC/AML policy for respondent payouts, GDPR compliance framework, and a history of reconciliation reports showing a one-to-one link between survey earnings and outbound payouts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Reliance on third-party payout rails such as PayPal Mass Payout and Wise for cross-border disbursements.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed EMI service agreement proving payment-account ownership, the EMI's CSSF or EU passport licence certificate, annual SOC/ISAE assurance reports, payout-threshold controls, segregation of safeguarded funds, and periodic reconciliation statements with identifiable counterparties.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound wires from non-resident investors and shareholders should be routed via SWIFT MT103/MT202 to a Luxembourg corporate account in the SCSp's legal name. The filing must state an EU Balance of Payments purpose code corresponding to 'capital participation' or 'direct investment' (e.g., code D for direct investment) rather than personal remittance. No prior BCL approval is required, but the receiving bank will expect an executed partnership agreement, board/partner resolution authorising the capital call, source-of-funds evidence from the remitting investor, and confirmation that the SCSp's RCS registration exactly matches the beneficiary name and account number.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade and operational settlements should use SWIFT MT103 for supplier payments, documentary collection and commercial letters of credit, with standby LCs issued by a Luxembourg credit institution where required. For consumer survey remittances and market-research panel rewards, the preferred compliant rails are SEPA credit transfers for EU/EEA payees and SWIFT MT103 for non-EEA payees, in both cases referencing a payment purpose such as 'market-research honorarium' or 'survey participant compensation'. Batch low-value disbursements may be executed through PayPal Mass Payout API and Wise Batch, provided the relevant EMI agreements, payout caps, and AML transaction monitoring are in place and reconciliation reports are retained.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Forward rate agreements entered with a Luxembourg-licensed credit institution for the sole purpose of hedging EUR/non-EUR cash-flow exposure

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual RCS data confirmation (Confirmation annuelle des données du Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés) — statutory annual verification/maintenance of the SCSp register entry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year; electronic confirmation must be completed before 31 December of each relevant calendar year (LBR sends an anniversary-based reminder; filing is made through the LBR e-Declaration portal).
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to complete the annual confirmation constitutes a contravention of the amended Law of 19 December 2002; court-assessed fines range from EUR 50 to EUR 5,000 with periodic coercive fines possible; persistent default after formal judicial/administrative injunction exposes the SCSp to administrative strike-off (radiation d'office) from the RCS.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual beneficial-ownership (UBO/RBE) confirmation — annual validation of the declared beneficial owners recorded for the SCSp
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least one confirmation per calendar year via the LBR e-Declaration portal; any cross-border or domestic transfer of limited partnership interests must first be notified as an event-driven update without undue delay and must then be covered by the next annual confirmation.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-confirmation or false confirmation is punishable under the amended Law of 13 January 2019 by criminal fines up to EUR 250,000 and imprisonment of up to six months for the general partner and responsible managers; repeated default may trigger the LBR administrative compliance procedure and strike-off of the RCS registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual accounts filing (dépôt des comptes annuels) — statutory financial statements filing where the SCSp has a corporate general partner or exceeds the small-undertaking exemption thresholds
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS); publication in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of approval of the annual accounts by the general partner/partners, and in any case no later than 10 months after the financial year-end (31 October for a 31 December year-end); exempt if all unlimited-liability general partners are natural persons.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or non-deposit exposes the general partner to fines of EUR 50 to EUR 5,000 plus coercive per-day penalties and judicial action; the commercial court may order compulsory filing, appoint a réviseur d'entreprises, and the Registrar may initiate administrative dissolution/strike-off after formal notice.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit by a Luxembourg réviseur d'entreprises agréé applies where: (i) the SCSp exceeds, on two consecutive balance-sheet dates, two of the three thresholds — total assets EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average 50 employees; (ii) a general partner is a corporate entity that itself requires an audit and consolidates the SCSp; (iii) the SCSp qualifies as a regulated AIF or fund vehicle subject to CSSF supervision; or (iv) partners or relevant stakeholders holding the statutory minority (generally 10%) validly request an audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as set out in the accounting chapter of the amended Law of 19 December 2002 (Plan comptable normalisé Luxembourg); IFRS as adopted by the EU is permitted; the fiscally transparent SCSp computes income at partner level, while any separately prepared statutory accounts follow the same Luxembourg GAAP framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SCSp, being without legal personality, is nonetheless an RBE-listed entity; the general partner must file event-driven UBO updates without undue delay upon any transfer, contribution, or change of limited partnership interests, and a full confirmation is due at least once per calendar year. The annual confirmation validates the existing beneficial-ownership structure and is not a substitute for the immediate filing required when a partner enters or exits or the percentage holding changes.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members, Register of Directors, Minute Book

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% aggregate for Luxembourg City companies (17% corporate income tax + 7% unemployment solidarity surcharge on the 17% + 6.75% municipal business tax on trading profits; municipal rate varies by commune from 6.75% to 10.01%)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SCSp is fiscally transparent unless it opts into full corporate taxation; partners are taxed directly in their home jurisdiction. Principal incentives: 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividend and capital-gain income (Art. 166 LIR), 80% IP Box deduction for eligible IP income (Art. 50ter LIR), 0% net wealth tax on corporate participations held by taxed entities, and exemption of the SCSp itself from net wealth tax when classified as a transparent partnership.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory time limit under Art. 110 LIR; carryback is prohibited; foreign permanent establishment losses remain limited to the local assessment period)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire 400 (Déclaration pour l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) filed electronically via the official eCDF e-filing platform of the Administration des contributions directes (ACD) using the corporate taxpayer matricule / RCSLU number; ancillary Form 509 tax return schedules (partnership allocation) apply for the transparent SCSp.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. Quarterly advance payments (acomptes) are simultaneously required on 10 March, 10 June, 10 September and 10 December of the current tax year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Paper returns: 31 May of the year following the fiscal year-end. Electronically filed returns via eCDF benefit from an automatic administrative extension to 31 December of the year following the fiscal year-end; for a non-calendar fiscal year the deadline runs from the close of the accounting period as notified in the assessment notice.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, RCSLU registration number, Luxembourg tax matricule, fiscal year, business address and legal form code for SCSp.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners must be identified by full legal name, registered address, tax identification number and percentage entitlement; the form must explicitly mark 'SCSp – fiscalement transparent' and attach the partnership agreement and a notarised register of partners.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Commercial net profit or loss per the audited financial statements before and after reclassification adjustments; reconciliation from accounting profit to taxable basis.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Because the SCSp is pass-through, this box must state that no corporate income tax is assessed at the entity level; the full commercial result is allocated pro rata to partners and separately reported on Form 509 schedules for each resident and non-resident partner.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption claims for qualifying dividends and capital gains; IP Box deduction calculations; interested-party transaction disclosures.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only income attributable to a Luxembourg taxable partner may benefit from Luxembourg exemptions; non-resident partners should not apply Luxembourg exemption provisions on the Form 400 but must rely on home-jurisdiction credit mechanisms supported by the Luxembourg allocation schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section D (Tableau des participations et bénéficiaires effectifs)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Group chart, direct and indirect shareholdings above 5%, ultimate beneficial owner declarations, and intercompany transaction schedule for transfer pricing documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The UBO disclosure requirement applies to all partners, including non-resident partners; a failure to list beneficial owners is an AML filing breach and can trigger a frozen assessment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of truthfulness and electronic signature by the manager, legal representative or authorised tax adviser; attachment index for financial statements, TP documentation and DTA-relevant certificates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident general partners may sign through a Luxembourg authorised fiscal agent; where no such agent exists, a written power of attorney must be filed with the ACD before the electronic return is accepted.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late or omitted Form 400 filing triggers (i) a statutory surcharge (majoration) up to 10% of the final tax assessed if the tax is paid late, (ii) late interest at 0.4% per month on the unpaid amount, (iii) administrative fines in the range of EUR 25 to EUR 250 for non-filing, and (iv) loss of the right to set off unused tax losses if the tax office proceeds to a discretionary assessment (taxation d'office).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% domestic Luxembourg withholding tax on dividends distributed by a resident company; reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive and Luxembourg domestic participation exemption where the corporate shareholder holds at least 10% of the capital for an uninterrupted period of 12 months; treaty rates for portfolio shareholders typically range from 5% to 15%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a Double Tax Agreement, the payee must (i) file a written relief request with the Luxembourg ACD using the official CRD/TRC application (Attestation de résidence fiscale), proof of residency being the foreign tax residence certificate or Form 33; (ii) obtain the Luxembourg tax residence certificate from the ACD generally within 10 business days; (iii) present the certified certificate to the withholding agent before the distribution for zero-rate or treaty-rate application; and (iv) where tax has been withheld at 15%, submit a reclaim within the five-year limitation period accompanied by the CRD, dividend voucher, UBO declaration and underlying share register. The Luxembourg DTA network (approx. 75 treaties) generally reduces dividend WHT to 5% or 0% for qualifying substantial holdings and provides 0% domestic exemption for interest and royalties.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg does not impose statutory withholding tax on cross-border interest or royalty payments to non-resident corporations; the domestic rate is 0%. Treaty rates where applicable are typically 0% for interest and royalties under the OECD model, although some treaties preserve a 10% royalty withholding cap; the 0% domestic treatment remains conditional on economic substance and on the absence of artificial routing under the Luxembourg GAAR and ATAD-compliant anti-abuse rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Master File must be prepared where the consolidated group turnover exceeds EUR 50,000,000; Local File is required where the Luxembourg entity's net annual turnover exceeds EUR 450,000 and controlled transactions exceed EUR 100,000 in aggregate, or where the ACD specifically requests comparable documentation under Art. 56 LIR. Arm’s-length benchmarking for the consumer panel SaaS platform must cover intangibles, marketing distribution, data licensing and platform services.
approved_arm_length_methodologies: CUP, Resale Price, Cost Plus, TNMM, Profit Split
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg has no standalone Economic Substance Regulation statute, but an SCSp must demonstrate genuine economic substance under the place of effective management test (Art. 14 LIR), the general anti-abuse provision (Art. 6 of the Steueranpassungsgesetz), the 2020/2021 ATAD-compliant anti-hybrid and exit-tax rules, and the substance-oriented administrative guidance of 2017/2018. For a cross-border consumer polling and market research platform, acceptable substance comprises a leased or owned physical office in Luxembourg, decision-making supervisory meetings in Luxembourg, qualified resident staff (operations, data-analytics, compliance), local bank accounts and merchant/PayPal-Wise settlement infrastructure, audited financial records and transfer pricing documentation updated annually. Absence of these elements can cause the ACD to disregard the Luxembourg residency and to reassess all platform revenue in the ultimate parent jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Wilful omission of partner-level taxable income allocation, submission of false Form 400s, concealment of survey-panel revenue settled via PayPal/Wise through offshore personal accounts of the general partner, or deliberate failure to disclose the ultimate beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 396 et seq. of the Abgabenordnung (AO) and criminal tax fraud provisions of the Luxembourg General Tax Code: fine between EUR 5,000 and EUR 50,000 per offence (up to five times the evaded amount in grave cases) and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years; in addition the statutory 10% surcharge, documented late interest, and forfeiture of all loss carryforwards.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and general partners are jointly and severally liable for the corporate tax shortfall where culpable breach of duties is proven; criminal conviction triggers automatic civil restitution, possible travel bans (interdiction de séjour / exit-control measures) pending sentencing, and imprisonment up to five years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating an SCSp as a pure booking shell with no Luxembourg office, zero resident employees, nominee partners, management decided entirely abroad, and routing 100% of the platform profit to a tax-haven shareholder through artificial fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reclassification of the SCSp as a fully taxable Luxembourg corporate entity; taxation of the entire recharacterised commercial margin at 24.94%; application of the anti-abuse penalty under Art. 6 StAnpG; restitution of all unpaid tax with 0.4% monthly interest; a fine of up to EUR 10,000 for failure to maintain substance records; and potential disqualification from the Luxembourg register of commercial entities.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the limited-liability veil: the general partner is personally liable for the unpaid CIT, net wealth tax and penalties of the shell to be assessed against it, civil seizure orders against private assets, and business-ban orders lasting up to 10 years in case of fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the survey-panel payout platform to launder proceeds or to facilitate round-tripping of funds to shell partners through PayPal Mass Payout or Wise transfers without performing customer due diligence on high-volume panel members and without registering the activity of payment services under the Law of 12 November 2004 (CSSF).
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: CSSF administrative sanctions under the amended AML Law of 12 November 2004 and Law of 29 July 2020: fines of up to EUR 5,000,000 or 10% of annual turnover whichever is higher; freezing of the entity's bank accounts by the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit; withdrawal of operating authorisations; closing of Wise and PayPal merchant accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Personal civil liability for all funds laundered where knowledge is established, professional disqualification orders, travel bans during criminal investigations, and imprisonment under the Luxembourg Criminal Code for money laundering (up to five years) with aggravated sentences where the predicate offence is committed abroad.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Basing intercompany charges for the consumer polling SaaS model on fabricated royalty or data-licensing fees designed to strip 100% of Luxembourg-sourced EBIT; absence of any local file or benchmarking study despite related-party transactions above the EUR 100,000 threshold; conclusion of the payout with no documented allocation of the arm's-length profit to the substantive Luxembourg operating partner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Art. 56 LIR: revaluation of all controlled transactions at arm's length; assessment of the full margin in Luxembourg with recharacterisation of the mis-invoiced fees as hidden distributions; a specific documentation penalty equal to 10% of the adjustment whenever the TP file is not produced or is materially deficient; and application of the strict burden of proof against the taxpayer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors signing intercompany contracts without economic substance expose themselves to joint-and-several liability for the primary adjustment under company law (Law of 10 August 1915, Art. 710-1) and, where the mispricing is deliberate, to criminal tax fraud liability with civil restitution and imprisonment; the Luxembourg tax authorities may also apply a statutory presumption of sham against the responsible officers.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate failure to file the Form 400 for the SCSp beyond the extended 31 December e-filing deadline, engaging the ACD's discretionary assessment (taxation d'office) powers and preventing the partner from claiming available participation exemptions or treaty relief.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Late return surcharge up to 10% of assessed tax, monthly late interest of 0.4%, administrative fine of EUR 25 to EUR 250 per return, and an automatic extension of the assessment period to 10 years in cases of omission or gross negligence versus the ordinary 5-year period.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The managing partner and any directors who cause the omission are personally responsible for the added penalties and the monetary interest accruing from the filing date; in cross-border cases the ACD may issue an enforcement order against the foreign assets of the general partner and request a freeze order under the EU Recovery Directive.
